claim: Fix \(h\in\mathbb N\), set \(k=h^2\), and for a positive integer starting value \(x_0\) let \(x_{n+1}=h^2/(x_0+\cdots+x_n)\), with \(x_n=a_n/b_n\) in lowest terms. Let \(F_h(x_0)\) be the number of indices \(n\ge2\) for which \((2/h)a_n+b_n\) is not a perfect square. Put \(P(h)=\{p\mid h: p=2\text{ or }p\equiv1\pmod4\}\), \(\alpha_p=v_p(h)\), and \(M_h=\prod_{p\in P(h)}p^{\alpha_p+1}\). For each \(p\in P(h)\), let \(T_p(t)=t+t^{-1}\) on \(\mathbb P^1(\mathbb F_p)\), with \(T_p(0)=T_p(\infty)=\infty\), and define \(B_{p,r}=\{t\in\mathbb F_p^*:T_p^r(t)=0\}\) and \(c_{p,r}=|B_{p,r}|\). Then the failed term indices are exactly \(\{r+1:\tau_p(x_0)=r<\infty\text{ for some }p\in P(h)\}\), where \(\tau_p(x_0)=r\) exactly when \(x_0\equiv p^{\alpha_p}(h/p^{\alpha_p})t\pmod{p^{\alpha_p+1}}\) for some \(t\in B_{p,r}\). Consequently \(F_h\) is exactly periodic modulo \(M_h\). If \(w_{p,r}=c_{p,r}\) and \(w_{p,\infty}=p^{\alpha_p+1}-\sum_r c_{p,r}\), then the natural density of starts with exactly \(j\) failed terms is the exact rational number \(\delta_j(h)=M_h^{-1}\sum_{\tau:\,|\{\tau_p<\infty\}|_{\mathrm{distinct}}=j}\prod_{p\in P(h)}w_{p,\tau_p}\), where the cardinality counts distinct finite hit times, so simultaneous obstructions from several primes contribute one failed term. For \(h=65\), the exact period is \(4225\) and the counts for \(j=0,1,2\) are \(3507,714,4\), respectively.

correctness.rationale: The proof separates the three p-adic starting regimes v_p(x_0)<v_p(h), =v_p(h), and >v_p(h). Only equality can produce a later divisor p|u_r. In that regime the reduced ratio modulo p evolves by t -> t+t^{-1}, and each finite first-hit t gives exactly one class modulo p^(v_p(h)+1). Pairwise coprimality of the relevant prime powers makes the local states independent by CRT; grouping by distinct hit times correctly handles simultaneous prime obstructions. The included verifier independently agrees with the theorem for all h<=60 over complete predicted periods and exhausts h=65.
